description: Starter cultural references for Graves World. Metadata and original study notes only; no copied protected expression.

entries.title: Spirited Away
entries.creator: Hayao Miyazaki / Studio Ghibli
world_applications: Give each town location a practical purpose and a lived-in history.
Let small acts of care change relationships over time.
entries.original_analysis: A strange world feels emotionally legible when its inhabitants have work, needs, boundaries, and ordinary routines. Wonder is strongest when it shares space with practical details.
entries.rights_note: Reference metadata and original analysis only; do not reproduce film scenes, characters, designs, or dialogue.

entries.title: The Lord of the Rings
entries.creator: J. R. R. Tolkien
world_applications: Give regions distinct histories, names, materials, and customs.
Make ordinary residents consequential to the fate of places.
entries.original_analysis: A convincing secondary world carries traces of older ages in its geography, language, ruins, songs, and everyday decisions. Scale is balanced by intimate relationships.
entries.rights_note: Reference metadata and original analysis only; no copied passages, maps, languages, or distinctive character designs.

entries.title: The Green Knight
entries.creator: David Lowery
world_applications: Use recurring objects to carry moral and historical meaning.
Build quests around choices and consequences rather than combat alone.
entries.original_analysis: Symbolic journeys gain force when tests reveal character rather than merely measure strength. Repeated visual motifs can let the audience interpret a world without exposition.
entries.rights_note: Reference metadata and original analysis only; do not reproduce film imagery, dialogue, or scene composition.

entries.title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
entries.creator: William Blake
world_applications: Let festivals and folk songs carry more than one interpretation.
Give the town poetry that asks questions instead of dictating answers.
entries.original_analysis: Contrasting perspectives can coexist in a culture. A simple symbol becomes richer when different residents understand it differently.
entries.rights_note: Blake's historical works are public domain in the United States; this archive stores original notes, not reproduced poems.

entries.title: Oral folklore and community storytelling
entries.creator: Many traditions and tellers
world_applications: Allow stories to change subtly as different residents retell them.
Create local customs with practical roots and multiple versions.
entries.original_analysis: Folklore belongs to communities, not a single authorial voice. Treat living traditions with context and respect; avoid flattening distinct cultures into decorative motifs.
entries.rights_note: Broad study category, not a license to appropriate specific living traditions; research origins and community context before adapting.
